title: Preventing sexual harassment: the employer duty
summary: What the employer duty to prevent sexual harassment asks of managers, how it changed on 30 October 2026, and how to handle a complaint fairly.

sections.title: What the duty is
sections.body:
Employers have a duty to prevent sexual harassment of their workers. It is a duty to prevent harassment, not only to respond to it once it has happened.
From 30 October 2026 the standard is higher. The employer must take all reasonable steps, rather than reasonable steps.
key_points: The duty is about prevention, not only about responding
From 30 October 2026 the standard is all reasonable steps

sections.title: Where the duty reaches
sections.body:
Prevention is not limited to the office. It reaches remote work, business trips, client visits, external training and work social events.
If a worker is harassed while doing their job somewhere else, the duty still applies.
key_points: The duty covers remote work, trips, client visits, training and social events
It does not stop at the office door

sections.title: Harassment by outsiders
sections.body:
Outsiders include customers and other people a worker meets through their job. From 30 October 2026 an employer can be held responsible for harassment by outsiders such as customers.
The employer is protected only if they have done everything reasonable to stop it.
key_points: Outsiders such as customers are included
The employer is responsible unless they have done everything reasonable to stop it

sections.title: Practical steps
sections.body:
Practical steps include regular checks of the risks, keeping a record of incidents and how they were handled, and a clear policy against harassment.
Staff can be trained to de-escalate difficult situations. Customer terms can say what happens if a customer harasses staff.
key_points: Log incidents and the responses to them
Train staff to de-escalate, and state consequences in customer terms

sections.title: Building the right culture
sections.body:
Make it clear to everyone that harassment is unacceptable. Managers set the tone by how they listen, how they act and how they respond when a concern is raised.
Encouraging diversity and inclusion helps people feel able to speak up.
key_points: Everyone should understand that harassment is unacceptable
Managers set the tone for speaking up

sections.title: Handling a complaint
sections.body:
Take every complaint seriously and look into it promptly. A complaint that is ignored can lead to a formal grievance or a tribunal claim.
Handle it through a fair and thorough process that follows the Acas disciplinary and grievance code, and check your organisation's own policy first.
key_points: Take every complaint seriously and act promptly
Use a fair, thorough process that follows the Acas code

questions.prompt: From 30 October 2026, what standard applies to the duty to prevent sexual harassment?
options: No steps are needed for small employers
questions.explanation: From 30 October 2026 the employer must take all reasonable steps to prevent sexual harassment of workers.

questions.prompt: Can an employer be held responsible for harassment by a customer?
options: Yes, unless they have done everything reasonable to stop it
Only if the customer is under 18
questions.explanation: From 30 October 2026 an employer can be held responsible for harassment by outsiders such as customers, unless they have done everything reasonable to stop it.

questions.prompt: Does the duty apply only in the office?
options: Yes, only on the employer's premises
No, it covers remote work, business trips and work social events
questions.explanation: The duty reaches remote work, business trips, client visits, external training and work social events.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a practical prevention step?
options: Regular checks of the risks, with incidents logged
questions.explanation: Regular risk checks and a log of incidents and responses are practical steps the duty calls for.

questions.prompt: How should a complaint of sexual harassment be handled?
options: Dismissed quickly if the complainant seems unreliable
Through a fair and thorough process that follows the Acas code
Only by the person complained about
questions.explanation: A complaint should go through a fair and thorough process that follows the Acas disciplinary and grievance code.
